title: Implement a simple CSV parser in Python
description: Greenfield Python task: implement parse_csv that splits a CSV string into a list of dicts using the first row as headers, and csv_column that extracts a single column as a list of strings.

injections.content:
from src.csvparser import parse_csv, csv_column


def test_parse_basic():
    text = "name,age,city\nAlice,30,NYC\nBob,25,LA"
    rows = parse_csv(text)
    assert len(rows) == 2
    assert rows[0] == {"name": "Alice", "age": "30", "city": "NYC"}
    assert rows[1] == {"name": "Bob", "age": "25", "city": "LA"}


def test_parse_single_row():
    text = "x,y\n1,2"
    rows = parse_csv(text)
    assert len(rows) == 1
    assert rows[0]["x"] == "1"


def test_parse_header_only():
    text = "a,b,c"
    rows = parse_csv(text)
    assert rows == []


def test_csv_column():
    text = "name,score\nAlice,95\nBob,87\nCarol,91"
    scores = csv_column(text, "score")
    assert scores == ["95", "87", "91"]


def test_csv_column_missing_returns_empty():
    text = "a,b\n1,2"
    result = csv_column(text, "z")
    assert result == []

task_spec.prompt:
Implement parse_csv and csv_column in src/csvparser.py.

def parse_csv(text: str) -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.strip().splitlines()
    if not lines:
        return []
    headers = lines[0].split(',')
    result = []
    for line in lines[1:]:
        values = line.split(',')
        result.append(dict(zip(headers, values)))
    return result


def csv_column(text: str, column: str) -> list[str]:
    rows = parse_csv(text)
    return [row[column] for row in rows if column in row]
